text:
carmen: Quick heads-up — after int8 bringup for ranker-v3 on holdout_x, we see MRR +1.9% but NDCG@10 -2.1%. small sample but odd. anyone free to triage? :thinking:

ben: oof. can you paste the eval command and a tiny output snippet?

carmen: running `./tools/eval_rerank --model=ranker-v3-int8 --cohort=holdout_x --k=10 --seed=42`
carmen: sample output:
```
MRR@10: 0.312 -> 0.318 (+1.9%)
NDCG@10: 0.412 -> 0.403 (-2.1%)
Top1 acc: 0.587 -> 0.602
Tail (rank 6-10) avg rel: 0.201 -> 0.175
```

alice: couple quick suspects: candidate ordering / nondet shuffling at batch boundaries, or a change in scoring rescaling (embed/score normalization). those can push top1 up while degrading tail ranks.

dinesh: +1 for ordering. we had a microbatching change in runtime last week that changed candidate batching heuristic. if candidate arrays get processed in different order the stable-tie handling can move docs around. can you check `SORT_CANDIDATES` in eval config?

carmen: checking now — harness config shows `sort_candidates: false` (weird, harness used to have it true). i didn't change harness. maybe build default changed.

ben: that would explain it. if you disable deterministic sorting, tiny score differences or tie-breaking can boost top hits but harm overall ranking consistency. try forcing `sort_candidates: true` and re-run on a small shard.

carmen: rerunning with `sort_candidates: true` now. kicked off: `job 38219`

ci-bot: Job 38219 started (eval_rerank, shard=3). link: https://ci.internal/jobs/38219 :rocket:

(eva a few mins later): ran shard 3 quick: new metrics:
```
MRR@10: 0.313 -> 0.317 (+1.3%)
NDCG@10: 0.412 -> 0.410 (-0.5%)
Top1 acc: 0.587 -> 0.598
Tail (6-10) avg rel: 0.201 -> 0.193
```

eva: delta smaller for NDCG but still negative. suggests ordering was part of it but not all.

dinesh: next suspect: length / doc normalization change in the scoring pipeline. did the score rescale patch (`scorer.normalize_len=true`) land in int8 runtime or in the model wrapper? tiny length smoothing can favor short docs and boost top1. can you diff the scoring code between the int8 and fp16 branches?

carmen: diff shows int8 branch sets `len_norm_power=0.07` while fp16 had `0.05`.

ben: that matches: slightly higher len penalty -> short docs boosted -> top1 up but tail degrades. can you try running with `len_norm_power=0.05` on the int8 build to isolate?

carmen: will do. started job 38222 with len_norm_power=0.05 (same shard).

ci-bot: Job 38222 started (eval_rerank, shard=3).

(eva later): results job 38222:
```
MRR@10: 0.312 -> 0.316 (+1.3%)
NDCG@10: 0.412 -> 0.411 (-0.2%)
Top1 acc: 0.587 -> 0.599
Tail (6-10) avg rel: 0.201 -> 0.196
```

eva: NDCG dip nearly recovered. looks like ordering + len_norm together explained most of it.

dinesh: good find. recommendation: 1) revert len_norm diff in int8 build (keep fp parity), 2) enable deterministic candidate sort in harness by default, 3) add a small unit test that runs eval on a microbatch boundary to catch nondet shuffles.

carmen: agreed. i'll open a PR with the len_norm revert + test. also let's add a short blurb in the bringup checklist to check `sort_candidates` and len_norm parity.

ben: thanks. one more thought — log the top-5 doc ids for a sample of queries in the rollout so we can detect this class of shift in canary quickly.

carmen: yup will add logging that emits sample top-5 for 1% of requests.

dinesh: nice. thanks for triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Job 38222 finished (success). artifacts: s3://ci-artifacts/38222/metrics.json

carmen: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rerank/pull/1423 — includes len_norm revert, harness default change, and the microbatch unit test. assigning to @dinesh for review.

ben: reviewing now. will +1 if tests pass.

carmen: closing note — keep an eye for skewed head vs tail when onboarding; metric splits are super helpful (top1 vs tail) rather than only aggregated ndcg/mrr.

alice: agreed. saved the sample scripts to detect this: `tools/compare_head_tail.py` (small helper).

carmen: thanks everyone!
